name: MIXING STUDIES (APTT)
interpretation:
Mixing studies are specialized tests used to evaluate the cause of prolonged APTT (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time). They help determine whether the prolongation is due to a clotting factor deficiency or an inhibitor (like lupus anticoagulant or a specific factor inhibitor).

Result of Mixing Study Interpretation Likely Causes
APTT Corrects (to normal or near-normal levels) Suggests clotting factor deficiency Hemophilia A (Factor VIII deficiency), Factor IX or XI deficiency
APTT Does NOT Correct (remains prolonged) Suggests presence of an inhibitor Lupus anticoagulant, specific factor inhibitors (e.g., anti-Factor VIII), heparin contamination
APTT initially corrects, then prolongs after incubation Suggests a time-dependent inhibitor Often seen in acquired Factor VIII inhibitors (e.g., in acquired hemophilia)

Correction = Factor Deficiency

  • The normal plasma provides the missing factor.

  • Common in:

    • Hemophilia A or B

    • Von Willebrand disease (if it affects Factor VIII stability)

    • Liver disease (mild cases)

No Correction = Inhibitor Present

  • The abnormal plasma has an antibody or inhibitor that neutralizes clotting factors even in normal plasma.

  • Seen in:

    • Lupus anticoagulant

    • Heparin contamination

    • Specific inhibitors (e.g., Factor VIII inhibitor in acquired hemophilia)

Methodology: Automated Coagulometer, Clot based Method.

Instrument: Instrumentation Laboratory – ACL elite PRO.

Test Significance: The activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) measures the functionality of intrinsic & common pathways of coagulation cascade.

Limitations of assay:

· Abnormalities of coagulation factor VII, factor XIII and platelets are not detected by this test procedure.

· Platelet factor IV, a heparin neutralizing factor can be released due to platelet aggregation or damage and may influence the test.

· Decrease in APTT time is observed in males under estrogen therapy and oral contraceptive administration in females.

. APTT based heparin therapeutic range is not established for this assay.

Comment: 1. If the prolonged aPTT is corrected in mixing study, it indicates factor deficiency (Factor VIII, IX, XI, Contact factors, rarely vWF disease).

  1. If prolonged aPTT is not corrected by mixing study, it is indicative for presence of specific factor inhibitor (Factor VIII, IX, XI, contact factors), Heparin and direct thrombin inhibitor.

Interpretation: Determination of APTT helps in estimating abnormality in most of the clotting factors of the intrinsic pathway including congenital deficiency of factor VIII, IX, XI, and XII and is also a sensitive procedure for generating heparin response curve for monitoring heparin therapy.

A mixing study is used to study the cause of a prolonged screening test. In a mixing study, platelet free normal plasma is mixed with the patient sample. In a 1:1 mix, one part patient sample is mixed with the one part of normal plasma and the mixture is tested immediately as well as after incubation of 1-2 hrs.
